mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals labor market weakness, which is expected to lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 1.5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it indicates a potential monetary tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the specified conditions are met but the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests supply chain issues, which could negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by more than 1% in a month
failure_condition: If industrial production declines but S&P 500 returns are positive over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which should positively impact related sectors and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 5% month-over-month
failure_condition: If housing starts increase by more than 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) and stable employment (PAYEMS) may indicate inflationary pressures that could lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and PAYEMS remains stable
failure_condition: If the specified conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) signals a robust labor market, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 10,000 jobs month-over-month
failure_condition: If employment growth exceeds 10,000 jobs but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A divergence between housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) may indicate an imbalance in demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the specified divergence occurs but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
